title: Community Biogas in Uganda: Programme Review and Lessons Learned 2023
summary: Review of household and community biogas programme implementation in Uganda, covering technology performance, adoption drivers, gender outcomes, and recommendations for scale.
description: This report synthesises learning from biogas programme implementation across Uganda over the 2018–2023 period, drawing on M&E data, household surveys, and qualitative case studies. Key findings include: fixed-dome digesters show superior durability and lower maintenance cost compared to floating-drum designs in Ugandan conditions; the most successful programmes used community enterprise models with local trained technicians; bio-slurry adoption as fertiliser significantly improved crop yields and represented a major non-energy benefit of biogas; household time savings — particularly for women — average 2–3 hours per day; and the main barriers to adoption include high upfront cost, requirement for livestock ownership, and limited awareness. The report includes an analysis of financing models and recommendations for the next phase of biogas scaling in Uganda.
